blindSummary:
This country has a strong progressive trajectory but a social climate that lags the law. It was the first in its region to legalise same-sex marriage (2024), approved a national LGBT+ equal-opportunities action plan in 2025 (with particular attention to trans people), joined 16 fellow members of its supranational union in urging another member state to revise its anti-LGBT laws, and hosted a Pride event in the capital in 2025. There are no documented severe traveler-axis incidents — no mob violence, trans-tourist rape, police-brutality, or foreign-trans-detention case.

The notable gap is legal gender recognition: it remains medical-gatekept (it requires a diagnosis and is "complicated, arbitrary"; a reform bill stalled), and surveys show residents are markedly more avoidant of public LGBTI visibility than the union-wide average (62% avoid holding hands; 40% avoid certain locations for fear of assault).

Bathrooms are unrestricted, there is no criminalisation, and the region's visa-free travel area poses no trans-specific border friction.
blindOutOfScope: No trans-specific travel advisory; general urban crime very low.
blindSourceSummaries: National broadcaster news site: this country approved a national LGBT equal-opportunities action plan - the government committed in 2024 and the plan was approved in 2025, with particular attention to trans well-being across education, healthcare and the legal system.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): the first country in its region with marriage equality (June 2023), including adoption; support for marriage equality rose from 34% (2012) to 53% (2023, 75% among under-30s); the 2025 action plan strengthens protections; civil society continues to advocate for self-determination-based legal gender recognition and hate-speech protections.

Crowd-sourced safety data: homosexuality legal, marriage legal, no censorship; legal gender change legal but requires medical diagnosis; no nonbinary recognition; no hate-crime protections; employment discrimination prohibited on SOGI; housing discrimination protections cover sexual orientation only; conversion therapy not banned; bathroom access protected. Residents showed the highest share of hiding being LGBTIQ at work of any of 30 regions in a union-wide survey.

A global transgender-rights legal barometer's time series for this country (2011-2024): legal gender recognition exists but requires physiological alteration and psychiatric diagnosis; hate speech/crime legislation does not include gender identity; workplace/housing/healthcare anti-discrimination laws include gender identity; no known murders of gender-identity minorities.

Trans and LGBTI umbrella organisations' compliance report (2018) on this country's implementation of a regional human-rights body's recommendation on measures against discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity: covers hate crimes and data collection, safety of LGBT people deprived of liberty, hate speech, association, expression, transgender-specific health and private-life issues, employment, education, housing, sports and asylum.

A regional LGBTI-rights organisation's annual review 2026 (covering 2025), chapter on this country: joined 16 union member states urging another member state to revise its anti-LGBTI laws; the foreign minister publicly supported the capital's Pride event and overseas missions flew rainbow flags; in December the country adopted a national action plan to strengthen LGBTI equality across education, healthcare, employment and the legal system.

The union's fundamental-rights agency's LGBTIQ survey III country sheet for this country (2024): 62% avoid holding hands with a same-sex partner (union average across 27 states: 53%); 40% avoid certain locations for fear of assault (union average: 29%); 38% are open about being LGBTIQ (union average: 51%); work discrimination below the union average (12% vs 19%).

Diaspora news site (July 2017): embassies of numerous foreign states accredited in this country issued a joint declaration supporting a 2017 regional Pride event in the capital - 'LGBTI rights are human rights'; affirms protection from violence and discrimination.

Local advocacy organisation's article (Oct 2021) marking seven years of the cohabitation law - the registered-partnership act's implementing provisions were never adopted, forcing same-sex couples into court; documents cases including registration of a marriage contracted in another member state and unequal treatment found unconstitutional - the gap between law and implementation.
blindLocalsOnly: The medical-gatekept LGR regime and its stalled reform bill are resident-facing.
blindTangential: Same-sex marriage legal since 2024 — relevant to trans visitors travelling with partners.
